summary: Reproduced; the recorded fix closes case 1 only. Case 1 (A batch 2, C batch 1, indices (1,1)): at the fix parent e14fa3cf22ff exl3_mgemm returned normally and wrote all 1024 elements of a second output slot beyond C (sentinels changed); at the fix ea62df9eee39 nothing was written beyond C. Case 2 (A batch 2, C batch 3, indices (1,3)): at both commits the call returned normally and C[2] reached max |911.5| against ~0.3 for C[0] and C[1], i.e. the kernel read a third A matrix that does not exist (here the script's poisoned third slot). The fix clamps batch sizes to the index count, which leaves bszm_out = 3 > bszm_in = 2 in case 2.
what_ran: repro.py calls the extension's exl3_mgemm binding directly (12 arguments) on physical GPU 1 with two random K=4 EXL3 matrices (k = n = 1024): case 1 with C a view of a sentinel-filled 3-slot buffer; case 2 with A a view of the first 2 slots of a buffer whose third slot is 1e3.
limits: Out-of-range accesses are observed inside the script's own larger allocations, so the extent of the read/write is shown, not a fault. The out-of-range indices read in case 1 is not separately observed. Direct native call; no Python caller passes these shapes.
